record.original_question: What is the correct way to generalize the chirality group from two-orbit polytopes to k-orbit polytopes?

evidence.quote: Problem 7. Determine the "correct" way to generalize the chirality group to k-orbit polytopes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract n-polytope P is a ranked partially ordered set whose maximal chains (called flags) satisfy the diamond condition and a connectedness axiom; its automorphism group Γ(P) acts freely on flags. A polytope is called regular if Γ(P) is transitive on flags, and (two-orbit) chiral if Γ(P) has exactly two orbits on flags with adjacent flags lying in different orbits. For a chiral polytope P, the chirality group X(P) is defined as the kernel of the natural epimorphism from Γ(P) onto the automorphism group of the maximal regular quotient of P; equivalently, X(P) measures how far P is from being regular and is trivial precisely when P is regular.

More generally, a polytope is called a k-orbit polytope if Γ(P) has exactly k orbits on the set of flags, and its symmetry type is encoded by a symmetry type graph on k vertices.

Problem. Formulate an appropriate definition of a "chirality group" for an arbitrary k-orbit abstract polytope P (for every k ≥ 2 and for every admissible symmetry type graph) that:
(i) reduces to the classical chirality group when P is a two-orbit chiral polytope,
(ii) is trivial if and only if P is regular,
(iii) measures, in a functorial way, the obstruction for P to cover its maximal regular quotient,
and establish its basic structural properties (such as its relation to the mix of P with its dual/mirror images and to coverings of P by regular polytopes).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on k-orbit abstract polytopes (e.g., work on automorphism groups of 3-orbit polyhedra and characterizations of k-orbit polytopes as coset geometries) develops symmetry-type-graph machinery and partial generalizations, but no source found gives a definitive, generally accepted notion of a chirality group for arbitrary k-orbit polytopes. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Automorphism groups of 3-orbit polyhedra
status_evidence.snippet: Necessary and sufficient conditions on generators of Γ to construct a polyhedron with 3 orbits on flags; suggests a way to generalize to any number of flag orbits.
status_evidence.claim: Generalizations beyond two-orbit chirality are still being developed; no canonical chirality group for k-orbit polytopes is established.

status_evidence.title: All polytopes are coset geometries: characterizing automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes via coset geometries and symmetry type graphs.
status_evidence.claim: k-orbit polytopes are an active area; chirality-group analogues are not formulated in this characterization.

status_evidence.title: Mixing chiral polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Defines and studies the chirality group of a chiral (two-orbit) polytope via mixing with its mirror image.
status_evidence.claim: The classical chirality group is defined only for two-orbit chiral polytopes.
